$\partial_mA_{m}=mA_{m}^{-1}$; see Section~\ref{sec:cift}.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- proposition-19: body_md -->
\label{prop:clean}
$\left\langle A_{m}^{-1}Q,\varphi\right\rangle=0$, and consequently $\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\varphi\,Q=0.$
<!-- end proposition-19 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
Pairing \eqref{eq:dmQeq} with $\varphi\in\operatorname{ker}L_{+}$ and using self-adjointness,
$0=\left\langle L_{+}\partial_m Q_m,\varphi\right\rangle=\left\langle \partial_m Q_m,L_{+}\varphi\right\rangle
=-m\left\langle A_{m}^{-1}Q,\varphi\right\rangle$, so $\left\langle A_{m}^{-1}Q,\varphi\right\rangle=0$. Substituting into
Corollary~\ref{cor:polluted} gives $\left\langle Q,\varphi\right\rangle=0$.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
\label{rem:d1}
As $m\to0^+$, $A_{m}^{-1}\to(-\Delta)^{-1/2}$. For $d\ge2$, $(-\Delta)^{-1/2}Q$ is bounded
($Q\in L^1\cap L^\infty$ with exponential decay), so the pairing is continuous up to
$m=0$. For $d=1$ the conclusion $\int\varphi Q=0$ is not obtained from
$\left\langle A_{m}^{-1}Q,\varphi\right\rangle$ but directly from scale invariance of $(-\Delta)^{1/2}$: at
$m=0$, $[(-\Delta)^{1/2},\mathcal E]=-(-\Delta)^{1/2}$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:scaling}
degenerates to $L_{+}\Lambda Q=-2Q^{p-1}+Q$ (the FLS identity), whence $\int\varphi Q=0$
immediately. Thus the clean relation holds for all $m\in[0,m_*]$.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Let $\mu_0:=Q(r_0)^{p-2}$, $r_0$ the sign-change radius from \eqref{eq:phi-sign}. Since
$Q$ is radially strictly decreasing and $p>2$, $Q(r)^{p-2}-\mu_0>0$ on $(0,r_0)$,
$=0$ at $r_0$, $<0$ on $(r_0,\infty)$; hence $Q^{p-1}-\mu_0 Q=Q(Q^{p-2}-\mu_0)$ has the
same sign pattern as $\varphi$, with strict inequality on $(r_0,\infty)$. Therefore
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sign-pos}
\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\varphi\,\big(Q^{p-1}-\mu_0 Q\big)\,dx>0 .
\end{equation}
On the other hand, by \eqref{eq:two-clean},
$\int\varphi(Q^{p-1}-\mu_0 Q)=\int\varphi Q^{p-1}-\mu_0\int\varphi Q=0$, contradicting
\eqref{eq:sign-pos}. Hence $\operatorname{ker}L_{+}\capL^{2}_{\mathrm{rad}}=\{0\}$.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:FC1}
The maps $A,P,S_m,K$ are $C^2$ on $(0,\infty)\timesH^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}$, with
$\partial_u S_m(u)=(A_{m}+1)u-\left|u\right|^{p-2}u=:F(m,u)$,
$\partial_u F(m,u)h=(A_{m}+1)h-(p-1)\left|u\right|^{p-2}h$,
$\partial_m F(m,u)=mA_{m}^{-1}u$. At $u=Q_m$, $\partial_u F(m,Q_m)=L_{+}$.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
$A$ is $C^\infty$ in $u$ and real-analytic in $m$ (symbol $\sqrt{\left|\xi\right|^2+m^2}$ analytic,
derivative $m/\sqrt{\left|\xi\right|^2+m^2}$ bounded). By $H^{1/2}\hookrightarrow L^p$, $P$ is $C^2$
with $\partial_u^2P(u)[h,k]=p(p-1)\int\left|u\right|^{p-2}hk$ bounded via H\"older
$(\tfrac p{p-2},p,p)$. Continuity in $(m,u)$ is Nemytskii continuity of
$v\mapsto\left|v\right|^{p-2}:L^p\to L^{p/(p-2)}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:Fcont}).
$\partial_m A=m\left\langle A_{m}^{-1}u,u\right\rangle$ from $\partial_mA_{m}=mA_{m}^{-1}$.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:nehari-mfld}
For $m>0$ and $Q=Q_m$, $\partial_u K(m,Q)\ne0$, so $\mathcal N_m$ is a $C^2$ hypersurface
near $Q$ with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tangent}
T_Q\mathcal N_m=\Big\{\xi:\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}Q^{p-1}\xi=0\Big\}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Using $A(m,Q)=P(Q)$ and $(A_{m}+1)Q=Q^{p-1}$,
$\left\langle \partial_uK(m,Q),\xi\right\rangle=2\left\langle (A_{m}+1)Q,\xi\right\rangle-p\int Q^{p-1}\xi=(2-p)\int Q^{p-1}\xi$; in
particular $\left\langle \partial_uK,Q\right\rangle=(2-p)\left\|Q\right\|_p^p<0$, so $\partial_uK\ne0$ and
\eqref{eq:tangent} holds.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:Kcompact}
$\mathcal K:H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}\to(H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}})^{*}$, $\left\langle \mathcal K h,\phi\right\rangle=(p-1)\int Q^{p-2}h\phi$, is
compact.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
$Q^{p-2}$ decays exponentially (Prop.~\ref{prop:decay}). Split $\mathbb{R}^{d}=B_R\cup B_R^c$. On
$B_R$: $Q^{p-2}$ bounded, $H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}(B_R)\hookrightarrow\hookrightarrow L^2(B_R)$; on $B_R^c$:
$\sup_{B_R^c}Q^{p-2}\to0$. Hence $\left\|\mathcal K h_n\right\|_{(H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}})^{*}}\to0$ for
$h_n\rightharpoonup0$.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:posdef-tan}
Assume $\operatorname{ker}L_{+}\capL^{2}_{\mathrm{rad}}=\{0\}$ holds at $(m,Q)$. Then there is $c_0>0$ with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:posdef}
\left\langle L_{+}\xi,\xi\right\rangle\ge c_0\left\|\xi\right\|_{H^{1/2}}^2\qquad\forall\,\xi\in T_Q\mathcal N_m .
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:morse}, $\left\langle L_{+}\xi,\xi\right\rangle\ge0$ on $T_Q\mathcal N_m$. If not coercive,
there is $\xi_n\in T_Q\mathcal N_m$, $\left\|\xi_n\right\|_{H^{1/2}}=1$, $\left\langle L_{+}\xi_n,\xi_n\right\rangle\to0$.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:Kcompact}, $\xi_n\rightharpoonup\xi_*$ with $\int Q^{p-2}\xi_n^2\to
\int Q^{p-2}\xi_*^2$. If $\xi_*=0$ then $\left\langle (A_{m}+1)\xi_n,\xi_n\right\rangle\to0$, impossible. So
$\xi_*\ne0$, $\xi_n\to\xi_*$ strongly, $\xi_*\in T_Q\mathcal N_m$,
$\left\langle L_{+}\xi_*,\xi_*\right\rangle=0$; as a constrained minimizer, $L_{+}\xi_*=\alpha Q^{p-1}$, and
pairing with $Q$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:LplusQ}) gives
$\alpha\left\|Q\right\|_p^p=\left\langle \xi_*,L_{+} Q\right\rangle=-(p-2)\int\xi_* Q^{p-1}=0$, so $\alpha=0$ and
$\xi_*\in\operatorname{ker}L_{+}\capL^{2}_{\mathrm{rad}}=\{0\}$, contradicting $\left\|\xi_*\right\|_{H^{1/2}}=1$.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:openness}
If \eqref{eq:posdef} holds at $m_0$ with constant $c_0$, then there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that
for $\left|m-m_0\right|<\varepsilon$ (along a $C^0$ selection $Q_m\to Q_{m_0}$),
$\left\langle L_{+,m}\xi,\xi\right\rangle\ge\tfrac{c_0}2\left\|\xi\right\|_{H^{1/2}}^2$ on $T_{Q_m}\mathcal N_m$.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
$L_{+,m}=(A_{m}+1)-(p-1)Q_m^{p-2}$: $m\mapstoA_{m}$ norm-continuous and $Q_m\to Q_{m_0}$ in
$H^{1/2}$ give $\mathcal K_m\to\mathcal K_{m_0}$ in operator norm $H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}\to(H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}})^{*}$; tangent
spaces $\{Q_m^{p-1}\}^\perp$ vary continuously. Perturbation of a coercive form on a
continuously varying finite-codimension subspace preserves coercivity with a slightly
smaller constant.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:Fcont}
$F(m,u)=(A_{m}+1)u-\left|u\right|^{p-2}u$ is $C^1:(0,\infty)\timesH^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}\to(H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}})^{*}$.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
Linear part clear. For $N(u)=\left|u\right|^{p-2}u$, by $H^{1/2}\hookrightarrow L^p$,
$\left\|N(u+h)-N(u)-(p-1)\left|u\right|^{p-2}h\right\|_{(H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}})^{*}}\le
C\left\|h\right\|_{H^{1/2}}\sup_{[0,1]}\left\|\left|u+\tau h\right|^{p-2}-\left|u\right|^{p-2}\right\|_{L^{p/(p-2)}}\to0$.
Continuity in $m$ is norm-continuity of $A_{m}$.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:cift}
Let $m_0\in[0,m_*]$ and $Q_{m_0}\in\mathcal G_{m_0}$ satisfy \eqref{eq:posdef}. Then there
are $\varepsilon>0$ and a $C^1$ map $m\mapsto Q_m\inH^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}$ ($\left|m-m_0\right|<\varepsilon$),
$Q_m\in\mathcal N_m$ a ground state, $Q_m|_{m=m_0}=Q_{m_0}$, with $\partial_m Q_m$
solving \eqref{eq:dmQeq} weakly.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
For $(m,\xi)$ near $(m_0,0)$, $\xi\in T_{Q_{m_0}}\mathcal N_{m_0}$, the equation
$K(m,t(Q_{m_0}+\xi))=0$ has a unique positive solution $t=t(m,\xi)$ near $1$ (since
$\partial_t K|_{t=1}=(2-p)\left\|Q_{m_0}\right\|_p^p\ne0$), $C^1$ in $(m,\xi)$. Set
$u(m,\xi)=t(m,\xi)(Q_{m_0}+\xi)\in\mathcal N_m$, $\Sigma(m,\xi):=S_m(u(m,\xi))$. Since
$S_m|_{\mathcal N_m}=(\tfrac12-\tfrac1p)P$, critical points of $\Sigma(m,\cdot)$ are
ground states. The $\xi$-Hessian at $(m_0,0)$ equals
$\left\langle L_{+,m_0}\cdot,\cdot\right\rangle|_{T_{Q_{m_0}}\mathcal N_{m_0}}$, a coercive isomorphism by
\eqref{eq:posdef}. The Banach IFT applied to $\partial_\xi\Sigma(m,\xi)=0$ yields a $C^1$
map $m\mapsto\xi(m)$, $\xi(m_0)=0$, hence a $C^1$ ground-state branch $Q_m$.
Differentiating $F(m,Q_m)=0$ in $m$ gives $mA_{m}^{-1}Q_m+L_{+}\partial_m Q_m=0$, i.e.\
\eqref{eq:dmQeq}. Exponential decay of $\partial_m Q_m$ follows from elliptic regularity
for $L_{+}$ (gap $m+1>0$) applied to the decaying right-hand side.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lem:posdef-tan-endpoint}
At $m=0$, \eqref{eq:posdef} holds.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
By \cite{FLS}, $\operatorname{ker} L_{+,0}\capL^{2}_{\mathrm{rad}}=\{0\}$ with Morse index one; the argument of
Lemma~\ref{lem:posdef-tan} applies unconditionally at $m=0$.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- proposition-20: body_md -->
\label{prop:F-C1}
$F:H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}\to(H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}})^{*}$, $\left\langle F(u),\phi\right\rangle=\left\langle A_{m} u,\phi\right\rangle+\left\langle u,\phi\right\rangle-\left\langle \left|u\right|^{p-2}u,\phi\right\rangle$,
satisfies $F(Q)=0$, $F\in C^1$, $DF(Q)=L_{+}$.
<!-- end proposition-20 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:Fcont} with $m$ fixed.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- proposition-21: body_md -->
\label{prop:Lp-iso}
Assume $\operatorname{ker}L_{+}\capL^{2}_{\mathrm{rad}}=\{0\}$. Then $L_{+}$ is a topological isomorphism.
<!-- end proposition-21 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Write $L_{+}=\mathcal A-\mathcal K$,
$\left\langle \mathcal A u,\phi\right\rangle=\left\langle A_{m} u,\phi\right\rangle+\left\langle u,\phi\right\rangle$. Then
$\left\langle \mathcal A u,u\right\rangle=\int(\sqrt{\left|\xi\right|^2+m^2}+1)\left|\hat u\right|^2\ge c\left\|u\right\|_{H^{1/2}}^2$, so
$\mathcal A$ is an isomorphism (Lax--Milgram). $\mathcal K$ is compact
(Lemma~\ref{lem:Kcompact}). Thus $L_{+}=\mathcal A(I-\mathcal A^{-1}\mathcal K)$ is Fredholm
of index $0$; injectivity ($\operatorname{ker}=\{0\}$) gives bijectivity, and the bounded inverse
theorem gives $L_{+}^{-1}$ bounded.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:local}
Assume $\operatorname{ker}L_{+}\capL^{2}_{\mathrm{rad}}=\{0\}$. Then there is $\delta>0$ such that if $U\inH^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}$ solves
$A_{m} U+U=\left|U\right|^{p-2}U$ weakly with $\left\|U-Q\right\|_{H^{1/2}}<\delta$, then $U=Q$.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
By Propositions~\ref{prop:F-C1}--\ref{prop:Lp-iso}, $F$ is $C^1$ with $DF(Q)=L_{+}$ an
isomorphism. The Banach inverse function theorem gives a neighbourhood $\mathcal U\ni Q$
on which $F$ is injective; $F(U)=0=F(Q)$ with $U\in\mathcal U$ forces $U=Q$.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{lem:levelbound}
There are $0<m_-\le m_+<\infty$ with $m_-\le m_m\le m_+$ for all $m\in[0,m_*]$, and
$m\mapsto m_m$ is continuous on $[0,m_*]$. Moreover $\left\|Q\right\|_{H^{1/2}}\le C$ and
$\left\|Q\right\|_p^p\ge C^{-1}$ uniformly, and for $m\in[\tfrac12 m_*,m_*]$,
$Q(x)\le Ce^{-\beta\left|x\right|}$ with $\beta=\tfrac12 m_*$.
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Uniform form equivalence: for $m\in[0,m_*]$,
$\int\langle\xi\rangle\left|\hat u\right|^2\le\int(\sqrt{\left|\xi\right|^2+m^2}+1)\left|\hat u\right|^2\le
(1+m_*)\int\langle\xi\rangle\left|\hat u\right|^2$, so $A(m,\cdot)\sim\left\|\cdot\right\|_{H^{1/2}}^2$
uniformly. Sobolev gives $P(u)\le CA(m,u)^{p/2}$; on $\mathcal N_m$, $A(m,u)=P(u)$, so
$A(m,u)\ge C_0>0$ and $m_m\in[m_-,m_+]$. Continuity: with
$m_m=\inf_u(\tfrac12-\tfrac1p)A(m,u)^{p/(p-2)}P(u)^{-2/(p-2)}$ and
$\left|A(m',u)-A(m,u)\right|\le C\left|m'^2-m^2\right|\left\|u\right\|_2^2$, one gets $m_{m'}\to m_m$. Uniform
decay: barrier/comparison for $A_{m}+1$ as in \cite[Prop.~3.10]{LZZ} (Hardy term absent).
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{lem:unif-K}
Let $m_n\to m$ in $[0,m_*]$ and $Q_n\in\mathcal G_{m_n}$ with $Q_n\to Q$ strongly in
$H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}$. Then $\mathcal K_n:\xi\mapsto(p-1)Q_n^{p-2}\xi\to\mathcal K$ in operator norm
$H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}\to(H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}})^{*}$.
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
For $\left\|\xi\right\|_{H^{1/2}},\left\|\phi\right\|_{H^{1/2}}\le1$,
$\left\langle (\mathcal K_n-\mathcal K)\xi,\phi\right\rangle=(p-1)\int(Q_n^{p-2}-Q^{p-2})\xi\phi$. Split
$\mathbb{R}^{d}=B_R\cup B_R^c$. On $B_R^c$, uniform decay (Lemma~\ref{lem:levelbound}) makes
$\sup_{B_R^c}(Q_n^{p-2}+Q^{p-2})\to0$; on $B_R$, $Q_n\to Q$ in $L^p\cap C^\alpha_{\rm loc}$
gives $Q_n^{p-2}\to Q^{p-2}$ in $L^d(B_R)\cap L^\infty(B_R)$. H\"older bounds both by
$\varepsilon$; the operator norm tends to $0$.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{lem:Lp-conv}
Under Lemma~\ref{lem:unif-K}, $L_{+,m_n,Q_n}\to L_{+,m,Q}$ in strong resolvent sense on
$L^{2}_{\mathrm{rad}}$, and $\left\langle L_{+,m_n,Q_n}\xi_n,\xi_n\right\rangle\to\left\langle L_{+,m,Q}\xi,\xi\right\rangle$ whenever
$\xi_n\to\xi$ in $H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}$.
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
$A_{m}[m_n]+1\toA_{m}[m]+1$ in strong resolvent sense (symbols converge monotonically), and
$\mathcal K_n\to\mathcal K$ in norm (Lemma~\ref{lem:unif-K}). Form convergence of the sum
follows; strong resolvent convergence is standard \cite{ReedSimonI}. The pointwise form
statement is immediate.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:proper}
If $m_n\to m$ in $[0,m_*]$ and $Q_n\in\mathcal G_{m_n}$, a subsequence converges strongly
in $H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}$ to some $Q\in\mathcal G_m$.
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
Pohozaev \eqref{eq:pohozaev} and level bounds give $\left\|Q_n\right\|_p^p\in[c_0,c_1]$, hence
$(Q_n)$ bounded in $H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}$. Radial compactness gives $Q_n\to Q$ in $L^p$, $Q\not\equiv0$.
Passing to the limit (mass term via strong resolvent convergence) gives $A_m Q+Q=Q^{p-1}$.
Strong $H^{1/2}$: $\left\|Q_n\right\|_p^p\to\left\|Q\right\|_p^p$ and Pohozaev transfer the other norms; norm
plus weak convergence gives strong convergence. Level continuity gives $S_m(Q)=m_m$, so
$Q\in\mathcal G_m$.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:localhomeo}
If $(m_0,Q_0)\in\mathscr{G}$ with $\operatorname{ker} L_{+,m_0}\capL^{2}_{\mathrm{rad}}=\{0\}$, then $\pi$ restricts to a
homeomorphism of a neighbourhood of $(m_0,Q_0)$ onto an interval, given by a $C^1$ branch.
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
$F(m_0,Q_0)=0$, $D_uF(m_0,Q_0)=L_{+,m_0}$ an isomorphism (Prop.~\ref{prop:Lp-iso}). Banach
IFT gives the $C^1$ branch and local uniqueness.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:coerc-limit}
Let $m_n\to m$, $Q_n\in\mathcal G_{m_n}\to Q\in\mathcal G_m$ strongly in $H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}$, and
$\textbf{(PD)}_{m_n}$ with $c(m_n)\ge c_*>0$. Then $\textbf{(PD)}_m$ holds at $Q$ with
constant $c_*/2$.
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
Let $\xi\in T_{m,Q}$, $\left\|\xi\right\|_{H^{1/2}}=1$. Define
$\xi_n:=\xi-\frac{\int Q_n^{p-1}\xi}{\int Q_n^{p-1}Q}Q\in T_{m_n,Q_n}$, well-defined for
large $n$ ($\int Q_n^{p-1}Q\to\left\|Q\right\|_p^p>0$). Since $\int Q_n^{p-1}\xi\to\int Q^{p-1}\xi=0$,
$\xi_n\to\xi$ in $H^{1/2}_{\mathrm{rad}}$. By $\textbf{(PD)}_{m_n}$,
$\left\langle L_{+,m_n,Q_n}\xi_n,\xi_n\right\rangle\ge c_*\left\|\xi_n\right\|_{H^{1/2}}^2$; letting $n\to\infty$ (form
convergence, Lemma~\ref{lem:Lp-conv}, $\left\|\xi_n\right\|_{H^{1/2}}\to1$),
$\left\langle L_{+,m,Q}\xi,\xi\right\rangle\ge c_*$. By homogeneity and compactness of $\mathcal G_m$,
$\textbf{(PD)}_m$ holds with $c(m)\ge c_*/2$.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:PD-implies-ND}
If $\textbf{(PD)}_m$ holds, then $\textbf{(ND)}_m$ holds.
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
$\textbf{(PD)}_m$ is the hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{thm:cift}, so $\partial_m Q_m$ exists,
giving $\left\langle A_{m}^{-1}Q,\varphi\right\rangle=0$ and $\int\varphi Q=0$ (Prop.~\ref{prop:clean}; for
$m=0$, Remark~\ref{rem:d1}) for any $\varphi\in\operatorname{ker} L_{+,m,Q}\capL^{2}_{\mathrm{rad}}$. With
$\int\varphi Q^{p-1}=0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:LplusQ}) and the oscillation theorem
(unconditional), the sign contradiction of \S\ref{ssec:signcontr} gives $\varphi=0$.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
\label{rem:PD-primary}
$\textbf{(PD)}$ is unconditional at $m=0$ (FLS), open (Lemma~\ref{lem:openness}), closed
(Section~\ref{sec:seam}), and implies $\textbf{(ND)}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:PD-implies-ND}) and
the branch (Theorem~\ref{thm:cift}). Thus $\textbf{(ND)}$ is a consequence, never a
hypothesis, of the continuation; the apparent circularity is removed. The oscillation
theorem, proved unconditionally, is available throughout.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- proposition-22: body_md -->
\label{prop:endpoint}
$\textbf{(PD)}_0$ holds.
<!-- end proposition-22 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
By \cite{FLS}, $\textbf{(ND)}_0$ holds and $L_{+,0}$ has Morse index one with the
negative direction transverse to $\mathcal N_0$; Lemma~\ref{lem:posdef-tan} (with $\xi_*=0$
forced by $\textbf{(ND)}_0$) gives $\textbf{(PD)}_0$.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- proposition-23: body_md -->
\label{prop:open}
If $m_0\in\mathcal M$ then $(m_0-\varepsilon,m_0+\varepsilon)\cap[0,m_*]\subset\mathcal M$ for some
$\varepsilon>0$.
<!-- end proposition-23 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:openness} (using $\textbf{(PD)}_{m_0}$, norm-continuity of $A_{m}$, and
$Q_m\to Q_{m_0}$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:proper}) gives $\textbf{(PD)}_m$ with constant
$\ge c(m_0)/2$ for $\left|m-m_0\right|<\varepsilon$.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- proposition-24: body_md -->
\label{prop:caseB}
If $m_n\in\mathcal M$, $m_n\to m\in[0,m_*]$, then $m\in\mathcal M$.
<!-- end proposition-24 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:PD-implies-ND}, $\textbf{(ND)}_{m_n}$ holds, so
$L_{+,m_n,Q_n}$ is a full-space isomorphism (Prop.~\ref{prop:Lp-iso}). We must show
$\textbf{(PD)}_m$.

\emph{Case A: constants bounded below.} If $\liminf c(m_n)=:c_*>0$, pass to a subsequence
with $c(m_n)\ge c_*/2$. For any $Q\in\mathcal G_m$, properness gives
$Q_n\in\mathcal G_{m_n}\to Q$; Lemma~\ref{lem:coerc-limit} gives $\textbf{(PD)}_m$ at $Q$
with constant $c_*/4$. As $Q$ was arbitrary and $\mathcal G_m$ compact,
$m\in\mathcal M$.

\emph{Case B: constants degenerate.} Suppose $c(m_n)\to0$; we derive a contradiction.
Along a subsequence there are $Q\in\mathcal G_m$ (limit of $Q_n\in\mathcal G_{m_n}$) and
$\xi_n\in T_{m_n,Q_n}$, $\left\|\xi_n\right\|_{H^{1/2}}=1$, with
$\left\langle L_{+,m_n,Q_n}\xi_n,\xi_n\right\rangle=c(m_n)+o(c(m_n))\to0$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:unif-K},
$\xi_n\rightharpoonup\xi_*$ with $\int Q_n^{p-2}\xi_n^2\to\int Q^{p-2}\xi_*^2$. If $\xi_*=0$ then
$\left\langle (A_{m}+1)\xi_n,\xi_n\right\rangle\to0$, impossible; so $\xi_n\to\xi_*$ strongly with
$\left\langle L_{+,m,Q}\xi_*,\xi_*\right\rangle=0$, $\xi_*\in T_{m,Q}$, $\left\|\xi_*\right\|_{H^{1/2}}=1$. The Lagrange
computation of Lemma~\ref{lem:posdef-tan} gives $L_{+,m,Q}\xi_*=\alpha Q^{p-1}$ with
$\alpha=0$, so $\xi_*\in\operatorname{ker} L_{+,m,Q}\capL^{2}_{\mathrm{rad}}$, $\xi_*\ne0$.

We now obtain the two clean orthogonality relations for $\xi_*$ at the limit, using only
convergent quantities.

\emph{First relation.} $\int\xi_* Q^{p-1}=\lim_n\int\xi_n Q_n^{p-1}=0$ (as
$\xi_n\in T_{m_n,Q_n}$, $\xi_n\to\xi_*$ in $L^p$, $Q_n^{p-1}\to Q^{p-1}$ in $L^{p'}$).

\emph{Second relation via the branch derivative.} By $\textbf{(PD)}_{m_n}$ and
Theorem~\ref{thm:cift} at $m_n$, there is $\dot Q_n:=\partial_m Q_m|_{m=m_n}$ solving
\begin{equation}\label{eq:branch-n}
L_{+,m_n,Q_n}\dot Q_n=-m_n A_{m_n}^{-1}Q_n .
\end{equation}
Pairing with $\xi_n$ (self-adjointness):
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pairing-n}
\left\langle L_{+,m_n,Q_n}\xi_n,\dot Q_n\right\rangle=-m_n\left\langle \xi_n,A_{m_n}^{-1}Q_n\right\rangle.
\end{equation}
Decompose $\dot Q_n=a_n Q_n+w_n$ with $w_n\in T_{m_n,Q_n}$. Then, using
$\left\langle L_{+,m_n,Q_n}\xi_n,Q_n\right\rangle=\left\langle \xi_n,L_{+,m_n,Q_n}Q_n\right\rangle
=-(p-2)\int\xi_n Q_n^{p-1}=0$,
\[
\left\langle L_{+,m_n,Q_n}\xi_n,\dot Q_n\right\rangle=\left\langle L_{+,m_n,Q_n}\xi_n,w_n\right\rangle.
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz for the nonnegative form on $T_{m_n,Q_n}$ and the upper bound
$\left\langle L_+ w,w\right\rangle\le C\left\|w\right\|_{H^{1/2}}^2$,
\[
\big|\left\langle L_{+,m_n,Q_n}\xi_n,w_n\right\rangle\big|
\le\left\langle L_{+,m_n,Q_n}\xi_n,\xi_n\right\rangle^{1/2}\cdot C\left\|w_n\right\|_{H^{1/2}}.
\]
Testing \eqref{eq:branch-n} against $w_n$:
$\left\langle L_{+,m_n,Q_n}w_n,w_n\right\rangle=-m_n\left\langle A_{m_n}^{-1}Q_n,w_n\right\rangle\le C\left\|w_n\right\|_{H^{1/2}}$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:levelbound}); by coercivity $c(m_n)\left\|w_n\right\|_{H^{1/2}}^2\le C\left\|w_n\right\|_{H^{1/2}}$,
so $\left\|w_n\right\|_{H^{1/2}}\le C/c(m_n)$. Hence
\[
\big|\left\langle L_{+,m_n,Q_n}\xi_n,\dot Q_n\right\rangle\big|
\le c(m_n)^{1/2}(1+o(1))\cdot\frac{C}{c(m_n)}=C\,c(m_n)^{1/2}(1+o(1))\to0 .
\]
By \eqref{eq:pairing-n}, $m_n\left\langle \xi_n,A_{m_n}^{-1}Q_n\right\rangle\to0$. Since $m_n\to m$ and
$\left\langle \xi_n,A_{m_n}^{-1}Q_n\right\rangle\to\left\langle \xi_*,A_m^{-1}Q\right\rangle$ (strong $\xi_n\to\xi_*$ in $L^{2}$,
norm-resolvent convergence $A_{m_n}^{-1}\to A_m^{-1}$ for $m>0$; for $m=0$ use
Remark~\ref{rem:d1} to get $\int\xi_* Q=0$ directly), we conclude for $m>0$
$\left\langle \xi_*,A_m^{-1}Q\right\rangle=0$, whence by Corollary~\ref{cor:polluted} applied to $\xi_*$,
$\int\xi_* Q=0$.

\emph{Contradiction.} With $\int\xi_* Q^{p-1}=0$, $\int\xi_* Q=0$, and $\xi_*$ changing
sign exactly once (Theorem~\ref{thm:osc}), the sign argument of \S\ref{ssec:signcontr}
gives $\int\xi_*(Q^{p-1}-\mu_0 Q)>0=0$, a contradiction. Hence $c(m_n)\not\to0$, Case B
is void, and by Case A $\textbf{(PD)}_m$ holds, i.e.\ $m\in\mathcal M$.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:M-all}
$\mathcal M=[0,m_*]$; consequently $\textbf{(ND)}_m$ holds for all $m\in[0,m_*]$.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
$\mathcal M$ is nonempty (Prop.~\ref{prop:endpoint}), open (Prop.~\ref{prop:open}), closed
(Prop.~\ref{prop:caseB}) in the connected $[0,m_*]$, so $\mathcal M=[0,m_*]$;
Lemma~\ref{lem:PD-implies-ND} gives $\textbf{(ND)}_m$.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:global}
For every $m\in[0,m_*]$, $\#\mathcal G_m=1$.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
By Corollary~\ref{cor:M-all}, $\textbf{(ND)}_m$ holds for all $m$, so
Lemma~\ref{lem:localhomeo} applies everywhere and $\pi:\mathscr{G}\to[0,m_*]$ is a proper
(Lemma~\ref{lem:proper}) local homeomorphism, hence a covering map. The fiber cardinality
is constant on the connected base and equals $\#\mathcal G_0=1$ (\cite{FrankLenzmann,FLS}).
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
By the scaling reduction (Section~\ref{sec:scaling}), uniqueness for \eqref{eq:main} is
equivalent to $\#\mathcal G_m=1$ for the normalized family, which is
Theorem~\ref{thm:global} (with $m_*$ arbitrary).
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
We proved in full: the sharp Green-kernel asymptotics (Proposition~\ref{prop:green}), the
spectral correspondence (Proposition~\ref{prop:spectral-corr}), the $C^1$ dependence
$m\mapsto Q_m$ without full-space invertibility (Theorem~\ref{thm:cift}), and the
$d=1$/$m\to0^+$ uniformity of the mass-covariance relation (Remark~\ref{rem:d1}). The only
external inputs are the strong maximum principle and Hopf lemma \cite{GT}, Aronszajn
unique continuation \cite{Aronszajn}, the extension theory \cite{StingaTorrea}, and the
massless endpoint uniqueness/nondegeneracy \cite{FrankLenzmann,FLS}.
<!-- end remark-8 -->
